report.description:
The rich proof report: per-step L1–L7 verdicts, the reached verdict, the
declared expectation, and the weakest-link grade.

Expectation.description:
The verdict a proof declares it expects at its close (`docs/spec/04` §5).

Externally tagged (`rename_all` only, no internal `tag`): the `FailsAt` and
`Unknown` newtype variants wrap a bare `String`, which serde's internal
tagging cannot merge a tag into — so this enum keeps serde's default
(external) representation, unlike the struct/unit-only [`ProofFinding`].

oneOf.description: `expect holds` — the casting should reach its close cleanly.
`expect blocked` — the casting should be blocked (by some failure).

`expect fails-at <error>` — the casting should fail at exactly this
declared error. A wrong argument that accidentally validates is a bug.

An `expect` clause naming a token that is not one of the three verdicts —
a typo silently reading as `holds` would gut the whole discipline
(`docs/spec/04` §5), so an unknown token is kept and refused, not coerced.

FileId.description: Identifier for a source file within a compilation.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

Ident.description: A named identifier with its source span.

span.description: Where the identifier appears in source.

ProofFinding.description:
A structural finding against a proof — a refinement of one of `L1`..`L7`, or
the meta-finding that the declared expectation was not met.

Two-channel like every load finding (charter koan 9): a stable machine
[`code`](ProofFinding::code) and a domain-spoken
[`message`](ProofFinding::message).

Internally tagged on `finding` (the house style for the fabric's data-carrying
finding enums — cf. `PracticeFinding` and `LoadFinding`): every variant is a
struct or unit variant, so the tag merges cleanly.

oneOf.description: L1 — a step names a form the practice does not declare.
L2 (*absent*) — a premise merely unestablished in the projection: a fizzle.
L2 (*contradicted*) — a premise the certain projection denies: a rebound.
L3 (*timing*) — a timing premise seated at the wrong phase: wrong-phase.

actual.description: The phase in force in the scene, if the scene established one.

cycle.description: The cycle whose phase was wrong.

oneOf.description: L4 — a form bound against an argument its parameters forbid.

binding.description: The binding key the form does not declare.

oneOf.description:
The proof header binds a role the practice does not declare. This is
malformed proof metadata, not an expected diegetic failure.

actor.description: The entity written as its filler.

oneOf.description:
L5 — a step joins premises by a law the practice does not license, or over
a premise it never established.

law.description: The law named (or `<unknown>` when a joined label does not resolve).

oneOf.description: L6 — a spend broke a resource's algebra law (overload is the affine case).

at.description: The step where the offending delta was applied.

code.description: The stable class of the breach.

message.description: The domain-spoken description from the resource algebra.

oneOf.description: L7 — the close does not follow from the accounted ledger.

The declared expectation was not met — most sharply, a proof that expected
a failure but *validated* (the silent-success bug the discipline catches).

L6 — a resource operation names a label that is not a declared resource
premise (an undefined label, or a world/timing premise). The accounting
cannot operate on a unit that was never declared.

L4 — a timing premise names a spoke the cycle does not carry
(`phase(tide, purple)` on `tide = ebb | slack | flood | high`): a
bad-instantiation, the phase equivalent of laying a figure on a leaf the
cycle has no room for.

The `expect` clause named a token that is not `holds`, `blocked`, or
`fails-at <error>` — a typo the discipline must refuse, not coerce to
`holds`.
The proof has no `close` — a casting with no conclusion cannot be judged.

The proof's header `in <practice>` names a practice other than the one it
was checked against; the verdict would be about the wrong law-set.

The direct AST header is not `<role> <actor> in <practice>`. Parser-backed
callers reject this earlier; the checker retains the invariant.

Captured proof clauses do not replay through the canonical surface and
parser. This protects direct AST callers from bypassing proof syntax.

diagnostics.description: Domain diagnostics returned by the real parser.

oneOf.description:
The proof does not carry exactly one final close. Parser-backed callers
reject this earlier; the checker keeps the invariant for direct AST users.

final_operation.description: Whether the sole close, when there is one, is the final operation.

oneOf.description: `premise <l> <atom> …` — an atom the casting rests on.
`assume <l> <atom>` — a fork-local supposition.
`step <l> instantiate <form> with …` — bind a form's parameters.
`step <l> chain from … by <law> conclusion <atom>` — join by a law.
`spend <l>` — draw a resource unit against a premise.
`release <l>` — return a conserved unit to the multiset.
`redistribute <l>` — move a conserved unit between accounts.
`reveal <l>` — surface a conserved unit already implied.
`close <atom> expect <verdict>` — the casting's conclusion.
A form the checker did not recognize (kept, never dropped — koan 4).

ProofReport.description:
The full report of checking one proof.

This is a frozen seam: `SERVE-1`'s `dli.check-ledger` and the payload battery
(PAY-2) consume it. The [`checks`](ProofReport::checks) flag is the one-bit
verdict — the proof is structurally valid and its declared expectation was
met — while
[`findings`](ProofReport::findings), [`verdict`](ProofReport::verdict), and
[`grade`](ProofReport::grade) carry the why, the where, and the strength.

checks.description:
Whether the proof checks: its shape is valid and its declared expectation
was met.

expectation_met.description: Whether the reached verdict met the declared expectation.

findings.description: The structural findings, ordered by the step where each fired.

grade.description: The weakest-link grade over the procedure chain (`Grade::weakest`).

speaker.description: The speaker named in the header (`speaker <who>`), if any.

verdict.description: The verdict the checker reached at the close.

ProofVerdict.description: What the checker made of the close, before the expectation is weighed.

oneOf.description: The close follows from the accounted ledger; nothing fired.

The casting is blocked at a structural class, with the practice's refining
error name (if one matched) and the step where it fired.

at.description: The label of the step where it failed.

class.description: The structural class the casting failed at.

error.description: The diegetic error this refines to, if the practice named one.

ResourceViolationCode.description: The stable class of a [`ResourceViolation`] (charter koan 9).

oneOf.description:
A linear or affine balance fell below zero — a unit was spent that was
never accounted (over-spend below the floor).

An affine balance rose above its declared capacity — more was held than
the cap allows.

A `linear conserved` multiset did not net to zero at the close — a step
minted or burned the resource.
A graded-monotone grade moved against its one declared direction.

Span.description: A half-open byte range within a single source file.

file.description: The file this span points into.

StepVerdict.description: One step's verdict in a checked proof.

grade.description: The grade this step contributes to the procedure chain.

label.description: The step's label (`p1`, `s2`), or the keyword for an unlabeled form.

note.description: A domain-spoken note (what the step did, or why it failed).

ok.description: Whether the step stands — no finding fired against it.

StructuralClass.description:
The seven structural error classes the checker knows.

Every diegetic failure a practice declares is a *refinement* of one of these
(`docs/spec/04-practices.md` §2). The classes are the closed target set that
well-formedness obligation 1 checks against: an `error` refining anything
else does not compile.

oneOf.description: L1 — unknown-form: the casting names a form the practice does not declare.
L2 — premise-not-available: a required premise is absent or contradicted.
L3 — side-condition: a declared condition fails (timing, consent, scope).
L4 — bad-instantiation: a form is instantiated against forbidden sorts.
L5 — invalid-chain: a step joins premises the law does not license.
L6 — resource-violation: a spend breaks the resource's algebra.
L7 — close-mismatch: the close does not follow from the accounted ledger.
